lesson.title: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
lesson.topic: Basic Radio Dispatching – Authority and Field Decisions
objectives: State the parameters of a radio dispatcher’s authority under Procedure 102.
Describe what dispatchers should do instead of making field decisions.
Apply the correct escalation path to field supervisors.
Apply the correct responses and prohibited actions listed in Procedure 102.

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102: What is the PURPOSE of this procedure?

choices.text: Define the parameters of a Radio Dispatcher’s authority

questions.solution: PURPOSE states it sets parameters of dispatcher authority.
questions.hints: Look at the PURPOSE line.

source.coverage: Parameters of a Radio Dispatcher’s authority.

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102: Dispatchers should be careful not to do what?

choices.text: Overstep their authority and make field decisions
Assign too few units to jobs

questions.solution: SCOPE warns dispatchers not to overstep authority by making field decisions.
questions.hints: Key phrase: overstep authority.

source.coverage: Do not overstep authority; assist field personnel with facts; refer to field supervisor; overtime response; examples where dispatcher takes control (road blocks/pursuit).

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102: In which situations may dispatchers be expected to take control?

choices.text: Assigning units to road blocks and pursuit situations

questions.solution: SCOPE gives road blocks and pursuit situations as examples.
questions.hints: Look for examples after 'such as'.

source.coverage: Do not overstep authority; assist field personnel with facts; refer to field supervisor; overtime response; examples where dispatcher takes control (road blocks/pursuit).

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102: What is the dispatcher’s primary duty to field personnel?

choices.text: Tell units what decision to make
Provide available facts and information needed to assess the situation properly

questions.solution: SCOPE states dispatchers assist by providing facts/information.
questions.hints: Think: information support, not decisions.

source.coverage: Do not overstep authority; assist field personnel with facts; refer to field supervisor; overtime response; examples where dispatcher takes control (road blocks/pursuit).

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102: If a field unit has difficulty making a decision, what should you do?

choices.text: Refer the unit to the field supervisor
Transfer the job to another dispatcher

questions.solution: SCOPE directs referring the unit to the field supervisor.
questions.hints: Look for 'refer that unit'.

source.coverage: Do not overstep authority; assist field personnel with facts; refer to field supervisor; overtime response; examples where dispatcher takes control (road blocks/pursuit).

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102: A unit asks, “Central are you authorizing overtime?” What is the appropriate response?

choices.text: Ask the unit to call back later.
Operational overtime is authorized by the patrol guide; you are to respond.
Yes, overtime is authorized by Central.

questions.solution: SCOPE provides the exact appropriate response.
questions.hints: This is quoted in the procedure.

source.coverage: Do not overstep authority; assist field personnel with facts; refer to field supervisor; overtime response; examples where dispatcher takes control (road blocks/pursuit).

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102: Which is an example of a field decision a Radio Dispatcher should NOT make?

choices.text: Order DARP without the unit’s request
Refer a decision to a field supervisor
Relay factual updates from a caller

questions.solution: RADIO DISPATCHER 1a gives ordering DARP without request as improper.
questions.hints: Look at example 1a.

source.coverage: Do not order DARP without unit request.

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102: What should the Radio Dispatcher NOT advise regarding a license check?

choices.text: Advise the unit to make an arrest

questions.solution: RADIO DISPATCHER 1b says not to advise an arrest re license check.
questions.hints: Example 1b is about arrests.

source.coverage: Do not advise a field unit to make an arrest regarding a license check.

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102 NOTE: Decisions in these examples should be made by whom?

choices.text: The field unit or patrol supervisor

questions.solution: NOTE says decisions should be made by the field unit or patrol supervisor only.
questions.hints: Look for 'field unit or patrol supervisor'.

source.coverage: These are examples; decisions belong to field unit or patrol supervisor only.

questions.topic: Procedure 102 – Dispatcher Should Not Make Field Decisions
questions.stem: Procedure 102 NOTE: If a unit requests a meal while several events are holding, what should the dispatcher do?

choices.text: Advise the patrol supervisor of the request
Place the unit out of service without notice

questions.solution: NOTE says advise the patrol supervisor when multiple events are holding.
questions.hints: This is a supervisor-notification rule.

source.coverage: Meal request when several events: advise patrol supervisor.
